summary.name: Maestro
summary.one_liner: Maestro is an open-source UI testing framework that runs human-readable YAML flows on iOS, Android and web apps, with a CLI, a desktop visual IDE (Maestro Studio), and a paid cloud service (Maestro Cloud) for scaling test runs.
use_cases: Automate end-to-end UI tests for iOS and Android apps
Run mobile test suites in CI pipelines
Let AI coding agents write and verify UI tests via MCP
Scale parallel test runs across simulators and emulators in the cloud
Record videos of test flows for demos and bug reports
Build tests visually in a desktop IDE
summary.what_it_does: Maestro lets you write UI tests as human-readable YAML flows that run against iOS Simulators and Android Emulators through the open-source CLI, using commands such as launching apps, tapping, inputting text, and asserting visibility. Maestro Studio is a visual IDE for Mac and Windows offering autocomplete, tap-to-generate YAML, selector inspection and an embedded emulator. An official Maestro MCP server exposes devices and commands to AI agents. Maestro Cloud runs suites in parallel across simulators and emulators and provides step-by-step video playback, logs and flake detection. The page also shows a sample AI-agent session generating a test plan for a settings screen, which is illustrative rather than a product feature claim.
notable: Open source CLI with human-readable YAML test flows
Official MCP server so AI agents can run and verify tests
Maestro Studio visual IDE with embedded emulator
Maestro Cloud parallel execution with video playback and flake detection
caveats: Maestro Cloud is a paid/hosted service; the page only describes it as a scale option and does not state prices
Maestro Studio is described for Mac and Windows; the CLI runs tests on local iOS Simulators and Android Emulators
Page lists web testing as supported but gives no details on how web tests are run
